differences.title: 1. SECURITY MODEL
differences.leftDesc: Deno requires explicit grants for network, file system, and environment access, enforcing a security-first mindset from the start.
differences.rightDesc: Bun aims for developer convenience with a more permissive default, though future security controls are planned. It prioritizes ease of use.

differences.title: 2. MODULE RESOLUTION
differences.leftDesc: Deno imports modules directly via URLs or import maps, promoting decentralized dependency management and explicit imports.
differences.rightDesc: Bun natively supports Node.js modules and npm packages, simplifying migration and leveraging existing ecosystems seamlessly.

differences.title: 3. BUILT-IN TOOLING
differences.leftDesc: Deno includes a formatter, linter, test runner, and bundler, offering a cohesive developer experience out-of-the-box.
differences.rightDesc: Bun bundles a fast bundler, transpiler, test runner, and package manager, aiming to replace multiple separate tools.

differences.title: 4. PERFORMANCE CORE
differences.leftDesc: Deno is built with Rust and utilizes V8 for its JavaScript engine, focusing on robust performance and safety.
differences.rightDesc: Bun is written in Zig and uses JavaScriptCore (from WebKit) for its engine, achieving remarkable speed through low-level control.

differences.title: 5. TYPESCRIPT SUPPORT
differences.leftDesc: Deno has built-in, first-class TypeScript support, treating TS as a primary language without separate compilation steps.
differences.rightDesc: Bun offers highly compatible TypeScript and JSX transpilation, integrating smoothly without requiring users to manage toolchains.

differences.title: 6. API DESIGN
differences.leftDesc: Deno champions web standards like Fetch API and Web Workers, aligning with browser APIs for consistency.
differences.rightDesc: Bun prioritizes Node.js API compatibility, enabling easy porting of existing Node.js applications and libraries.

differences.title: 7. ECOSYSTEM INTEGRATION
differences.leftDesc: Deno's URL-based imports encourage a decentralized module ecosystem, reducing reliance on central registries.
differences.rightDesc: Bun's strong npm compatibility allows direct use of the vast existing npm ecosystem, fostering rapid development.
